title: CSQ Unit 1 · Think Like a Robot (3-5)

items.q: A list of steps a robot follows in order is called…
Which block takes Bolt one square ahead?
Plan A uses 5 blocks. Plan B uses 12 blocks. Both reach the gem and keep Bolt safe. Which plan is better?
choices: Plan B, more blocks is always better
Plan A, it does the same job in fewer steps
Neither, both plans reach the gem
Plan B, longer plans are safer

items.q: The level asks for every gem. Route A and Route B both reach the flag. Route A misses one gem. Route B gets every gem but uses 3 more blocks. Which route is right?
choices: Route A, fewer blocks always wins
Route B, it does everything the level asks
Either, they both reach the flag
Neither, the gems do not matter

items.q: Bolt faces along the top row. The flag is below, down the left side. Which program starts toward the flag?
items.why: Turning first aims Bolt down the left side toward the flag. Moving first would run along the top row, away from the flag.

items.q: What does the block "turn left" do to Bolt?
choices: spins Bolt in place to the left
makes Bolt pick up a gem
items.why: A turn block only spins Bolt on the spot. Only a move block changes Bolt's square.

items.q: Route A takes 9 blocks and keeps Bolt dry. Route B takes 6 blocks but crosses a puddle. Which route should Bolt take?
choices: Route B, because it uses fewer blocks
Either one, because both reach the flag
Route B, because the puddle is only one square
Route A, because it keeps Bolt dry
items.why: Route B is shorter, but it gets Bolt wet. Safe comes first: a long dry route beats a short wet one, so Route A wins.

items.q: Which word means "do the same steps again"?
Which program moves Bolt 8 squares with the fewest blocks?
items.why: One repeat block holding one move, run 8 times, moves Bolt 8 squares with just two blocks.

items.q: How many squares does repeat 3 { move, move } take Bolt?
items.why: Each run of the repeat moves Bolt 2 squares, and it runs 3 times: 3 times 2 is 6.

items.q: Bolt should move 4 squares, but he spins in place 4 times and stays put. What is the bug?
choices: the turn is inside the repeat, not the move
the repeat number is too small
the move should come before the repeat
the program needs one more turn
items.why: The turn sits inside the repeat, so Bolt spins 4 times and never moves. Put the move inside the repeat instead.

items.q: A block that lets Bolt choose what to do is…
You do not know where the walls are. Which program never bumps a wall?
choices: if path ahead: move, else: turn left
items.why: Checking before each move means Bolt only steps when the way is clear, and turns when it is not. A loop of plain moves still bumps the first wall.

items.q: What is the difference between "when" and "if"?
choices: when runs once at the start; if runs at the end
they are the same block with two names
when is for gems; if is for walls
when waits for something to happen; if checks now
items.why: An if block asks its question right now. A when block waits and reacts the moment something happens.

items.q: "when a gem is picked up: open door". When does the door open?
choices: the moment Bolt picks up a gem
at the start of the program
items.why: A when block watches the whole program and fires the moment its event happens: the pick-up itself.

items.q: A labeled box the program can look in and change is a…
What does "change score by 1" do?
items.why: Change adds to what is already in the box. Set would replace it; change by 1 makes it one bigger.

items.q: gems is 0. Bolt picks up 3 gems; each time "change gems by 1" runs. What is gems now?
items.why: Each pick-up runs the change once, adding 1. Three pick-ups add 3 to 0, so gems is 3.

items.q: What does "set lives to 3" do?
choices: counts how many lives there are
puts exactly 3 in the lives box
items.why: Set puts exactly the value you name into the box, whatever was there before.

items.q: Breaking a big job into smaller parts is called…
Changing part of a program someone else made so it does something new is called…
Which of these is a remix?
choices: writing every step yourself on a blank grid
deleting a block you do not like
changing a classmate's My Block so it also opens the door

items.q: Bolt must cross four identical rooms. What is the smart move?
choices: write out every step four times in a row
make one My Block: Room and call it 4 times
use one very long move block
items.why: The four rooms are the same job four times. One named block, called 4 times, does it without writing it all out.

items.q: Which group of steps most deserves its own named block?
choices: the very first step of the program
a single turn in the middle
steps that repeat in several places
items.why: A named block earns its name when the same steps show up again and again in different places.

items.q: You take a My Block the game gives you that crosses one room, and add a gem pick-up to it. What have you made?
choices: a copy with nothing new in it
a remix: the old block plus something new
a bug in the old block
items.why: Starting from a block that exists and adding something of your own is a remix.
